paper_metadata.title: Structural Transformations in High-Strength Magnetically Hard Fe–Cr–Co–W–Ga Alloys
paper_metadata.journal: The Physics of Metals and Metallography

evidence.quote: The alloys based on the Fe–Cr–Co system that are alloyed with tungsten and gallium represent a new direction in the development of hard magnetic materials

The alloys were melted in an induction furnace in an argon atmosphere from pure charge materials (with a purity no less than 99.95%).
After homogenization at 1200°С for 2 h, the ingots were hot-forged at 1100–1150°.
The hot-rolled sheets were quenched from 1150°С for α solid solution
The hot-rolled sheets were quenched from 1150°С for α solid solution, and then the alloys were subjected to cold rolling with deformations to 60%.

The heat treatment for the high-coercivity state was performed at temperatures characteristic of the alloys of this type [4], i.e., at 620–640°С for 20–45 min and then at 600°С for 30–60 min.
After quenching from 1150°С, the high-temperature α-Fe–based solid solution was the only phase in all the alloys except for the alloy containing 0.5 wt % Ga

The samples aged after quenching from 1150°С without preliminary deformation were coarse-grained (100–200 μm).
The cold rolling of the samples quenched from 1150°С led to a strong grain refinement and a sharp drop in the amount of the γ phase or even to its complete disappearance.

mechanisms.name: precipitation decomposition of high-temperature solid solution

evidence.quote: the high-coercivity state in the alloys of this system is obtained due to the precipitation decomposition of the high-temperature α-Fe–based solid solution with the formation of a modulated structure
the high-temperature solid solution decomposes into three phases: an α1 phase enriched in Fe and Co; an α2 phase enriched in Fe and Cr; and a W-rich paramagnetic phase.
Owing to numerous deformation-induced defects, diffusion is accelerated, which favors an enhancement in the decomposition into the α1 and α2 phases

mechanisms.name: hindering of chromium diffusion by gallium

evidence.quote: This means that gallium hinders diffusion of chromium from the strong magnetic phase.
